findings.title: Exterior doors D-M-ENTRY, D-M-PORCH, D-S-BALCONY keep their RO base on the joist top while the subfloor is 0.75 in higher: sill, pan and drain strips sit inside the continuous subfloor in the model, A-513.2 draws it cut back

evidence.measured: Subfloor 0..0.75 in over the whole door footprint (deck_voids contain none of the sill points; deck edge at the sheathing face). W-M-N3 frame_base 0.75 vs RO bottom 0.0. D-M-ENTRY: sill bottom 0.50 in (0.25 in into the sheet), drain strips 0.06..0.60 in, threshold top 2.000 in = 1.25 over subfloor, 0.974 over LVP (1.026), 2.0 over landing FS-BW-FLOOR (0.0). D-M-PORCH: sill base 0.876, strips 0.06..1.105, threshold top 2.251 = 1.50 over subfloor, 1.225 over LVP, 1.31 over FS-SG-PORCH (0.94). D-S-BALCONY: pan 120.000..120.375 wholly inside the 120.0..120.75 sheet, sill outline top 121.897 = 1.15 over subfloor, 0.397 over oak (121.5), 1.02 over FS-SG-BALCONY near edge (120.879). Cut-back footprint: RO width (38.4 / 63.3 / 63.3 in) x about 5.8 in (frame 4.6 in for BALCONY).
evidence.expected: A sill pan needs a flat, level, solid bearing (SureSill FAQ/install guide cited in the note); a model that keeps the subfloor under the pan is a 0.25..0.75 in interference, a cut-back leaves the pan bearing on rim/blocking only. Whichever the owner chooses, model, A-513.2 and A-601's RO sill must say the same: re-seating on the subfloor lifts every threshold 0.75 in (ENTRY 2.75 over joist top: 1.72 over LVP; BALCONY 1.15 over oak) and the head 0.75 in.
